item.text: {"confident":true,"explanation":"A quadratic form is positive semidefinite when all eigenvalues of its symmetric matrix are nonnegative. I has eigenvalues 0 and 1, so it qualifies. II has a negative eigenvalue, −1, so it does not. III has eigenvalues 10 and 10, so it is positive-definite and also positive semidefinite.
